# PLLM

Private LLM inference documentation. Public weights; provider follows the protocol.

- [Use the Agents SDK](/pllm/docs/client/agents/): Keep the Responses endpoint and tracing inside your chosen trust boundary.
- [Chat from the terminal](/pllm/docs/client/chat/): Prepare while idle, then stream over the client-to-inference path.
- [Configure the client](/pllm/docs/client/configuration/): Separate inference, preparation, inventory, cache, and timeout settings.
- [Install the client](/pllm/docs/client/install/): Build the current public client from this source with UV and Maturin.
- [Follow a response](/pllm/docs/client/lifecycle/): Commit, prepare, reserve, batch prefill, decode, and burn safely.
- [Use the OpenAI SDK](/pllm/docs/client/openai/): Point standard Responses clients at a trusted local gateway, never inference.
- [Python SDK](/pllm/docs/client/python/): Prepare explicit inventory, then use a Responses-shaped local client.
- [Deploy with Docker](/pllm/docs/deployment/docker/): Run the three-role loopback topology and understand what it does not prove.
- [Deployment overview](/pllm/docs/deployment/overview/): Place three trust roles, route two online transports, and size inventory safely.
- [Publish the documentation](/pllm/docs/deployment/site/): Validate and export a static site with no inference endpoint.
- [Deploy with systemd](/pllm/docs/deployment/systemd/): Install separate inference and preparation services with explicit caches and secrets.
- [Start here](/pllm/docs/): Offline prepared inventory, online masked inference, and a local Responses boundary.
- [Run your first prepared request](/pllm/docs/quickstart/): Start inference and preparation, seal an inventory, and generate locally.
- [CLI reference](/pllm/docs/reference/cli/): Current public-path commands, role-specific flags, and legacy boundaries.
- [Compatibility and limits](/pllm/docs/reference/compatibility/): Current implemented surfaces, validation scope, and unsupported behavior.
- [Live protocol dashboard](/pllm/docs/reference/dashboard/): Run current source end to end and interpret its observed metrics.
- [Project structure](/pllm/docs/reference/development/): Build and test the Rust core, Python runtime, and current docs independently.
- [Build and release](/pllm/docs/reference/releasing/): Use committed locks, verified native artifacts, and scoped publication permissions.
- [Troubleshooting](/pllm/docs/reference/troubleshooting/): Diagnose role, inventory, timeout, transport, and checkpoint failures safely.
- [How PLLM works](/pllm/docs/research/architecture/): A local Responses interface around a private matrix protocol.
- [Benchmarks](/pllm/docs/research/benchmarks/): Read the workload and denominator before reading the speedup.
- [Executable BFV Mask Preparation for Public-Weight Language-Model Inference: A Historical PLLM Study](/pllm/docs/research/paper/): Historical executable study of BFV-prepared additive masks for public-weight integer linear layers.
- [Reproduce the study](/pllm/docs/research/reproduce/): Keep the experiment environment separate from the serving runtime.
- [Implementation roadmap](/pllm/docs/research/roadmap/): The next work follows measured costs, not a new model architecture.
- [Security boundaries](/pllm/docs/security/): Protected values, visible metadata, required trust, and unsupported claims.
- [Install the services](/pllm/docs/server/install/): Build the Rust extension and validate a public checkpoint source.
- [Model support](/pllm/docs/server/models/): Separate tensor import, graph execution, public bundles, and quality evidence.
- [Rust execution core](/pllm/docs/server/native/): Maturin packaging, exact integer kernels, thread policy, and evidence limits.
- [Measure and tune](/pllm/docs/server/performance/): Separate cold inventory, compact prefill, persistent decode, and local boundaries.
- [Run both services](/pllm/docs/server/usage/): Serve a public transformer body and preload committed corrections.
- [Research history](/pllm/research/): PLLM protocol research from the BFV bridge to offline prepared inference.
- [PLLM whitepaper](/pllm/whitepaper/): A two-page decision brief for prepared private inference.
